description: nf-core/taxprofiler context, aligned to the pinned 2.0.1 schemas. Taxonomic classification and profiling of shotgun metagenomic reads against classification databases.

databases.help: The database sheet (tool, db_name, db_params, db_path) taxprofiler requires. The user names the databases (see required_user_params) or the curated list in reference_bundles.json does; configure_run writes databases.csv into the run folder. An absolute path to a .csv is the user's own sheet on Luria and passes through. No database is provisioned on Luria.

run_kraken2.help: Kraken2 k-mer classification. Set from the databases: on for every classifier the sheet holds a database for, unless the question names particular classifiers (then only those). Needed by Bracken.

run_bracken.help: Bracken species abundance re-estimated from Kraken2, for a question about relative abundance. Set when the sheet holds a bracken database (kraken2 then runs on it too). Short reads only: taxprofiler skips it for long reads.

run_metaphlan.help: MetaPhlAn marker-gene profiles (bacteria, archaea, eukaryotes, species level). Set when the sheet holds a metaphlan database and the question does not name other classifiers.

run_motus.help: mOTUs marker-gene profiles, including species without a reference genome. Set when the sheet holds a motus database.

run_kaiju.help: Kaiju protein-level classification, for divergent or poorly referenced communities. Set when the sheet holds a kaiju database.

run_centrifuge.help: Centrifuge classification. Set when the sheet holds a centrifuge database.

run_diamond.help: DIAMOND protein alignment against a reference protein set (read 1 only for unmerged pairs). Set when the sheet holds a diamond database.

run_malt.help: MALT alignment, used for ancient or low-abundance pathogen screening. Set when the sheet holds a malt database.

run_krakenuniq.help: KrakenUniq, which adds unique k-mer counts to tell real hits from false positives (pathogen screening). Set when the sheet holds a krakenuniq database.

run_ganon.help: ganon classification and abundance. Set when the sheet holds a ganon database.

run_kmcp.help: KMCP profiling, including viruses. Set when the sheet holds a kmcp database.

run_sylph.help: sylph genome-level abundance (not standardised by TAXPASTA). Set when the sheet holds a sylph database.

run_melon.help: Melon, for long-read prokaryotic profiles (not standardised by TAXPASTA). Set when the sheet holds a melon database.

run_metacache.help: MetaCache classification (not standardised by TAXPASTA). Set when the sheet holds a metacache database.

run_profile_standardisation.help: TAXPASTA: one standardised table per classifier and database with a column per sample. Set when the question compares samples, or compares classifiers or databases, in one table; those tables come back into NExtSEEK as run-level Taxonomic Profile rows. The release's default (off) leaves only each tool's own per-sample reports.

run_krona.help: Krona interactive pie charts per classifier and database, for a question that wants to browse each sample's composition. The release's default is off.

perform_shortread_qc.help: Adapter clipping and length filtering of short reads (fastp) before classification. Set for raw Illumina reads, which is what a D.SEQ record holds unless it says the reads were trimmed; leave it unset for reads already trimmed.

perform_longread_qc.help: Adapter trimming and length/quality filtering of Nanopore or PacBio reads before classification. Set for raw long reads (an OXFORD_NANOPORE or PACBIO_SMRT instrument_platform).

perform_shortread_complexityfilter.help: Removes low-complexity reads, which inflate false-positive hits in Kraken-style classifiers. Set when the question is pathogen or low-abundance taxon detection, where false positives matter most.

perform_runmerging.help: Merges the runs of one sample before profiling, so each sample gets one profile. configure_run sets it when a sample can arrive as several runs (two rows share a sample, or a row downloads an experiment accession); with one run per sample the release's default stands.

perform_shortread_hostremoval.help: Removes reads that map to the host genome before classification. Set for host-associated samples (gut, skin, tissue, blood) when the question is about the microbes, and give hostremoval_reference; taxprofiler stops without it.

perform_longread_hostremoval.help: Host-read removal for long reads, set on the same grounds as perform_shortread_hostremoval; needs hostremoval_reference.

hostremoval_reference.help: The host genome FASTA on Luria (for example the human or mouse reference genome FASTA), required when either host-removal flag is set.

multiqc_title.help: MultiQC report title, when the user wants the report named.

required_user_params.name: databases
required_user_params.definition: The classification databases to profile against, one per line as CLASSIFIER PATH [PARAMS], with the database's full path on Luria. taxprofiler ships no database, and none is provisioned on Luria, so they must already exist there (a directory or a .tar.gz). Classifiers: kraken2, bracken, metaphlan, motus, kaiju, centrifuge, diamond, malt, krakenuniq, ganon, kmcp, sylph, melon, metacache. Every classifier you list runs, unless you ask for particular ones. If you already have a taxprofiler database sheet on Luria, give its full path instead.

pipeline.name: nf-core/taxprofiler
pipeline.core_rule: Columns: sample, run_accession, instrument_platform, fastq_1, fastq_2, fasta (the first six, in this order). sample, run_accession and instrument_platform are required. One row per D.SEQ run; sample is the D.SEQ UID; run_accession is its archive run accession, else the UID again; instrument_platform comes from the record's sequencing metadata (param atlas).
pipeline.reference_requirement: NONE from the genome bundles: taxprofiler classifies against the databases in its --databases sheet, and declares no genome, fasta or gtf parameter.

validation_rules: The sheet is comma-separated and opens with sample,run_accession,instrument_platform,fastq_1,fastq_2,fasta.

instrument_platform is one of the ENA platforms (ILLUMINA, OXFORD_NANOPORE, PACBIO_SMRT, BGISEQ, DNBSEQ, ION_TORRENT, ...). It only tells taxprofiler short reads from long ones: OXFORD_NANOPORE and PACBIO_SMRT are long, the rest short. A Nanopore or PacBio row leaves fastq_2 empty.
(sample, run_accession) must be unique; an experiment accession that downloads as several runs gets each run's accession.
A classifier runs only when its run_<tool> flag is set AND the database sheet names a database for it. run_bracken needs run_kraken2: taxprofiler stops at validation otherwise.
Host removal (perform_*_hostremoval) needs hostremoval_reference, or taxprofiler stops at validation.
taxpasta_add_* need taxpasta_taxonomy_dir (a taxdump), which is not staged on Luria, so they are not offered.
No classification database is provisioned on Luria: every run uses databases the user names, until reference_bundles.json lists staged ones.
notes: Recommended upstream: short and long reads in separate runs, each with its own database sheet (docs/usage.md). Bracken is skipped for long reads. sylph, melon and metacache profiles are not standardised by TAXPASTA.

report_writer_guidance.purpose: Build an nf-core/taxprofiler sheet from a resolved D.SEQ cohort of shotgun metagenomic libraries.
report_writer_guidance.workflow_role: Selected for 'what organisms are in these samples' on shotgun (not amplicon) reads.
population_priority: One row per D.SEQ leaf; sample = the UID.
instrument_platform from the leaf's data-driven verdict (resolve_samples data_driven_params).
Ask for the databases unless the curated list names some; say none is provisioned on Luria.
final_checks: Every row has sample, run_accession and instrument_platform.
Every classifier that runs has a database in the sheet.

runtime.basis: First guess from typical nf-core runtimes on one 16-CPU Luria node (Nessie's default submit); not yet measured on Luria. Loading a large Kraken2 database dominates and repeats per task.
runtime.setup_label: unpacking the classification databases (a .tar.gz database is unpacked in every run)
